summary: Audit of official evacuation data for the 47 lower-48 states outside California and for national alert channels, as of 2026-10-22, revised after an independent review. The round-2 decisions in BRIEF-3 answer most of the first pass's questions. IPAWS: no registration, so live alerts are those the NWS relays and past days use the OpenFEMA archive. Washington is the only partial state used, if it loads reliably. Florida is not shown, and county feeds are out of scope. Oregon OEM 'Evacuation Areas Public' is the one available statewide feed: live, empty off-season, licence 'Public'. The revision found that its last_edited_date is an OEM recalculation time, not an issue time, and that half of its 2026 history rows have no fire name. Washington's TLS failure has a root cause: the server sends only its leaf certificate. With DigiCert's public intermediate added for that one host, verification stays on and the layer reads live: 583 rows, 73 Active, only 5 of them with a level (68 automated rows must be filtered). Its licence includes an indemnification clause, which is open user question Q-A (recommended default: build it switched off until the user accepts). Arizona stays 'none' on firmer evidence: DEMA's statewide zones are a planning layer, not edited after 2026-02-12, while its counties sent 7 fire alerts in 2026. 44 state web searches are now logged. There are two blockers in today's code. The backend queries Cal OES outside California. The web's California rectangle gives 11 border places (Reno, Carson City, Stateline, Las Vegas, Klamath Falls, Ashland, Brookings, Yuma, Lake Havasu City, Bullhead City, Tijuana) an implied check: 'No evacuation order or warning listed here · Cal OES · not an all-clear'. There is also a latent bug: evac_status_key('No Evacuation Order') == 'order', and Washington's layer has that wording. The audit gives one additive adapter shape: per-source times and behaviour, the reason code state_not_available, border dedup, CA/OR/WA field mappings, a local-alerts kind per decision 5, 12 prioritised changes, a verification path for builders and a 47-row state table.

known_issues: Washington: whether the 4 manual 'Hatch Grade' Level 3/2 rows (Active since 2026-09-30) are still in force could not be confirmed (news results were undated or conflicting). This is the staleness the 'may be out of date' label warns about. The WA leaf certificate expires 2026-11-26: re-check the chain when it renews (R10, R11).
Oregon's live layer was empty in both passes (off-season). Live-shaped field behaviour is inferred from OEM's 2026 history layer, which snapshots the live layer every 5 minutes.
Oregon gives only a level number. Fire-3d renders 'Level N' plus OEM's published definition, flagged status_verbatim: false.

Oregon's terms basis is the one-word licence 'Public' on OEM's items plus the StoryMap's stated intent to share with the public. No disclaimer or redistribution text was found (omls.oregon.gov could not be reached).
IPAWS/OpenFEMA counts are CAP identifiers. 'Fire-related' includes burn bans, Red Flag notices and 5 tests sent as Actual, so the counts are an upper bound.

Per-state 'none' rests on ArcGIS Online searches, an owner review and one logged web search per state. A state server not registered in ArcGIS Online (like Washington's) could be missed, so R11 proposes a periodic re-check (Arizona in season).

The audit is 639 lines (target 150-250). The 47-row state table, the CA/OR/WA mapping, the complete Cal OES file list asked for by the review, the verification path and the evidence log make up most of it.
No browser run in either pass: the evidence for the border-rectangle blocker is an offline run of today's web model fed the backend's real answer shape, not a screenshot.
